parts:
Hello,

I'm trying to adjust a model for a binomial spatiotemporal series, but I encounter the error I paste below. I don't understand quite well what's going wrong. 

I've succesfully made other models with only spatial, only temporal RE and both effects without the interaction. My explained variable, AT (as can be seen in the code attached, you can reproduce the error with all those files, mind the folder names on the code) has some NAs values. 

I've tried to assign initial values or to train a dummy model, but I keep getting the same error over and over. 

I'm on a personal PC with 8 GB RAM, an intel core i5 7th gen, 2 GB of grapphic card, 69GB out of 1021 GB of internal storage used, and Windows 10 HOME, 64 bits. 
I use R version 4.5.0 (2025-04-11 ucrt) and installed INLA like a month ago.

Any idea? Thanks in advance.

parts:
Hi again,

I found two issues with the code:

1. You're feeding a raw matrix of coordinates to inla.spde.make.A that includes a non-coordinate column as the first column.
  This means that all the location calculations will be incorrect; in this case all of them are outside the mesh:
> sum(abs(proj.mat))
[1] 0
  Below, I've solved that by explicitly extracting the LON/LAT coordinates (in that order, as that's the order you used in the mesh creation).
  A better solution would be to store the data as an `sf` object (including any relevant crs information etc) as the code would then know how to access the coordinates, and whether they need to be transformed to some other coordinate system, etc.

2. You're saying that you have 153 groups, but your group indices go from 121 to 273.
  Subtract 120 from yearday when calling inla.spde.make.A, and that should solve that issue

coordinates.all.year <- as.matrix(df[,c("STAID","LAT","LON")])
rownames(coordinates.all.year) <- NULL

# spde things
# FL: extract correct coordinates, and use correct 1-based group indices
proj.mat=inla.spde.make.A(mesh=mesh, loc=coordinates.all.year[,c("LON", "LAT")],
                          group=df$yearday-120, n.group=153,
                          repl=df$year,n.repl=65)

Finn

Btw,
you may want to consider whether you really need a daily resolution of the yearday model, as the total model is quite large:

> fmesher::fm_dof(mesh)*length(unique(df$year))*length(unique(df$yearday))

Perhaps an ar1 model on the coefficients of an fm_mesh_1d(knots, boundary="free", degree = 2) mesh would be sufficient?
(Note: that kind of model would be easy to setup in inlabru, but I would not want to debug any such code in plain INLA...)

Finn
